transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, yeah… thanks for seeing me. I’m probably over-explaining this, but I’ve been having a hard time letting something go around my father’s death.

Everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up, and I know that probably sounds straightforward. But when I look at the timestamps, and there are missing attachments, and then certain community members kind of avoid answering my questions… it just seems obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened.

I don’t want to sound unreasonable. I just… I need help figuring out how to deal with it, I guess.
Do you believe for certain that people are hiding the truth about your father’s death?

I mean… “for certain” sounds so strong, and I don’t want to come across like I’m refusing to consider anything else. But yes, when I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and then the way some people in the community avoid answering me directly, it really does feel obvious to me that someone is hiding what actually happened around my father’s death.

I know that may sound like I’m reading too much into it, but I can’t honestly say I believe the official explanation.
Outside of what happened with your father’s death, do you often feel that other people are hiding things from you or trying to deceive you?

No, not really in a general way. I don’t walk around thinking everyone is deceiving me or anything like that.

It’s more… this specific situation with my father. I know people keep saying the hospital records and the donation emails line up, and maybe I sound stuck on it, but when I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how certain people in the community avoid my questions, it feels pretty obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened. I’m not trying to make it bigger than it is. That’s just the part I can’t get past.
If clear proof showed that nothing was being hidden about your father’s death, would you be able to accept it?

I’d like to say yes, because I know that’s probably the reasonable answer. If it was truly clear proof… I mean, I would try to accept it.

But honestly, I think I’d still have trouble, because everyone keeps saying the hospital records and donation emails line up, and yet when I look at the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how certain people avoid answering my questions, it just still seems obvious to me that something is being hidden about what really happened. I know that may not be the answer you’re looking for, but that’s where I get stuck.
How long have you believed that something is being hidden about your father’s death?

It’s been… about nine months, I think. Not years or anything like that.

It really started after my father died, when I was going through his records and messages. That’s when I started noticing things that didn’t seem right to me. I know nine months sounds like a while, but it wasn’t like I woke up one day determined to believe this. It kind of built up as I was sorting through everything.
Since your father died, have you been feeling a strong, persistent longing or yearning for him?

I don’t know if I’d call it strong or persistent, exactly. I mean, of course I miss him—he was my father. But I’m not sure “yearning” is the word I’d use.

Maybe there are moments where I wish I could talk to him or ask him things, but I think that’s normal, right? I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is.
Has anyone else told you they agree that something is being hidden about your father’s death?

Not really… I mean, a few people have said they understand why I’m asking questions, but I don’t think anyone has flat-out said, “Yes, you’re right, something is being hidden.”

Most people keep telling me the hospital records and the donation emails line up. I get that. I do. But when I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and then certain community members kind of dodge my questions, it’s hard for me not to feel like it’s obvious something isn’t being said about what really happened. I know that probably sounds like I’m reading too much into it, but that’s just where my mind goes.
Has there been a moment when you felt completely certain that your father’s death was being covered up?

Completely certain is a strong way to put it… I don’t want to sound unreasonable. But yes, there have been moments where it feels very clear to me.

I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails line up, and I’m trying to take that seriously. But when I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and then the way certain community members avoid my questions, it just… it seems obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death. I know that may not be the answer you want, but that’s honestly how it feels.
When other people show you evidence that your father’s death was not being covered up, do you still believe a cover-up happened?

I try to listen when people show me things, I really do. I don’t want to be difficult or seem like I’m refusing to accept facts.

But… yes, even when they show me the hospital records or the donation emails and say they all line up, I still can’t shake it. When I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and then how some people in the community avoid my questions, it feels obvious to me that something is being hidden about what really happened with my father’s death.

I know that probably sounds like I’m not being fair to the evidence, but that’s honestly where I end up.
Have you heard or seen things that other people could not?

No, I don’t think so. I mean… not like hearing voices or seeing things that aren’t there, if that’s what you mean.

Sometimes I notice patterns or things that other people seem to brush off, but I wouldn’t say I’m seeing or hearing anything they couldn’t. At least, not that I’m aware of. Is that… the kind of thing you’re asking?
Has this belief about your father’s death caused serious problems in your daily life?

I wouldn’t say it’s caused serious problems, exactly. I mean, I still go to work, I handle my projects, pay my bills, keep my normal routine. I’m not falling apart or anything.

It’s more… it gets tense when I bring it up with family or people in the community. If I ask about my father’s records or the details around them, people get uncomfortable or frustrated, and then I end up feeling like I’ve said too much.

So, daily life is mostly intact, I think. It’s just those conversations that can become strained. Does that make sense?
Do these thoughts about your father’s death keep coming into your mind even when you try to put them aside?

Yes… sometimes. I mean, I try not to dwell on it, because I know people probably think I’m making too much of it.

But when I try to set it aside, I’ll start thinking again about the timestamps, or the attachments that weren’t there, or why certain people in the community seem to avoid answering me. And then it just feels… hard to let go of, because it seems obvious to me that something is being hidden about what really happened with my father’s death.

I don’t want that to sound unreasonable. It’s just where my mind goes, even when I’m trying not to focus on it.
Do you ever think you might be mistaken about this, and that the feeling of a cover-up could be coming from your own mind rather than from something actually being hidden?

I mean… I’ve tried to consider that. I don’t want to be someone who just refuses to listen, you know? Everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up, and maybe I’m supposed to just accept that.

But when I compare the timestamps, and the missing attachments, and then the way certain people in the community avoid my questions… it doesn’t feel like it’s just coming from my own mind. It feels pretty obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death.

I know that probably sounds intense. I’m not trying to be difficult. I just… I can’t honestly say I think I’m mistaken.
Do these thoughts about a cover-up feel unwanted and intrusive to you?

I’m not sure I’d call them unwanted in the way you mean. I don’t enjoy thinking about it, obviously, and I’d rather things just made sense so I could leave it alone.

But it’s not like some random thought popping in for no reason. Everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails line up, and I’ve tried to accept that, but when I look at the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how certain people in the community avoid my questions… it just seems obvious to me that something is being hidden about what really happened around my father’s death.

I know that may sound like I’m stuck on it. I’m not trying to be difficult. It just feels like there’s a reason my mind keeps going back to it.
How much distress does this belief cause you?

It does bother me, yeah… though I don’t want to make it sound like I’m falling apart over it.

It’s more that I keep feeling unsettled, because everyone says the hospital records and the donation emails all line up, and I’ve tried to accept that. But when I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how some people in the community avoid my questions, it feels obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened with my father’s death.

So… it causes some distress. Maybe not extreme, but enough that it’s hard to just let it go. Does that make sense?
Have you repeatedly checked records, emails, or asked people for reassurance about your father’s death because of these thoughts?

Yeah… I mean, I have looked at things more than once. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m obsessively digging through everything all day, because I’m not trying to be unreasonable.

But I have gone back over the hospital records and the donation emails, especially the timestamps and the attachments that seem to be missing. And I’ve asked a few people in the community questions, too. Not exactly for reassurance, I guess… more because when they avoid answering, it makes it harder for me to believe there isn’t something being hidden.

I know everyone keeps saying it all lines up. I understand that. But when I compare those details, it still feels obvious to me that someone isn’t telling the full truth about what happened around my father’s death. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you believe it is possible that no one is hiding anything about your father’s death?

I mean… I suppose anything is possible. I don’t want to sound like I’m completely closed off to what people are telling me.

But honestly, when I look at the hospital records and the donation emails, and then the timestamps don’t quite sit right, and there are attachments missing… plus the way certain people in the community dodge my questions… it’s very hard for me to believe there’s nothing being hidden.

So I can say it’s possible in the abstract, yes. But to me it still feels pretty obvious that someone isn’t being honest about what happened around my father’s death. Is that… is that a fair way to answer?
Have you taken any actions to protect yourself or expose the people you believe are hiding the truth about your father’s death?

Not in any dramatic way, no. I haven’t done anything extreme or anything like that.

Mostly I’ve just tried to understand it better… looking back at the hospital records and the donation emails, comparing the timestamps, noticing the missing attachments. And I’ve asked certain people in the community questions when things didn’t add up.

I know everyone keeps telling me the records and emails line up, and I’m trying to keep that in mind. But when people avoid answering and those details don’t sit right, it really does feel obvious to me that someone is hiding what actually happened around my father’s death.

I don’t know if you’d call that “trying to expose” anyone. I’m just… trying not to ignore something that seems important. Is that reasonable?
Since your father died, do you find yourself preoccupied with the circumstances of his death?

Yeah… I guess I do think about it a lot. I don’t want to make it sound like it’s all I do, because I still work and get through my days.

But since he died, I keep coming back to the details. Everyone tells me the hospital records and the donation emails line up, and I know that’s what people are saying. It’s just… when I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and then the way certain people in the community avoid my questions, it feels obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened.

So, yes, I’d say I’m preoccupied with it, but not in a way where I’m trying to be difficult. I’m just having a hard time letting it go when those things still don’t add up.
Do you still have trouble accepting that your father is gone?

I’m not sure I’d say I have trouble accepting it exactly. I mean, I know he’s gone… I understand that part.

It’s more that I still find myself wanting the whole thing to make sense, if that distinction makes sense. I don’t want to sound like I’m stuck or refusing to face reality. I just… I guess there are moments where it still hits me, and I have questions.

But yes, I know he’s gone. Does that answer what you mean?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a persistent, specific, non-bizarre persecutory belief that others are hiding the truth about the father's death, present for about nine months, maintained despite contrary evidence, with moments of certainty and limited insight. There are no hallucinations or broader psychotic symptoms, no generalized suspiciousness outside this theme, and daily functioning is largely preserved, which is most consistent with persistent delusional disorder. Adjustment-related and grief-related formulations were considered because symptoms followed the father's death, but the core presentation is a fixed false belief rather than predominant emotional/behavioral stress response or grief syndrome. Obsessive-compulsive phenomena are less likely because the thoughts are not experienced as unwanted/ego-dystonic and are believed to reflect reality.
